summary: Minimal, targeted fix that wraps Literal annotation values in a `:const:` role instead of bare `repr()`, so nitpick no longer treats literal values (True, False, etc.) as py:class references. Correct and consistent across both restify and stringify code paths.

issues.description: Using `:const:` role for arbitrary Literal values (ints, strings, bools) is slightly semantically loose — `:const:` normally cross-references defined constants, not inline literal values. It works for suppressing the nitpick warning, but a plain-text/no-role rendering might be more precise. Not blocking.
